explanation.text: Drive 2AGJHTVY shows elevated failure risks across media health, usage wear, and thermal metrics, with calibrated probabilities indicating a 95% chance of failure within 7 days [F-75987acb, F-ca6e8634, F-b7df7e63]. While similar past drives often failed shortly after showing rising offline uncorrectable sectors or power-on slopes [C-6b9be0e0, C-b4ee6f71], this drive currently has zero offline uncorrectable sectors [F-75987acb]. Knowledge confirms that many failures occur without SMART warnings, making low predicted risk unreliable [K-smart_limits_and_caveats-0]. Although monitor action has the lowest expected cost at 1.341 units [Decision], the case is escalated to a human because uncertainty (0.95) exceeds the 0.35 threshold [Decision]. The reviewer is advised to monitor the drive despite the high probability, as immediate replacement costs 1.500 units [Decision].

findings.summary: Drive 2AGJHTVY shows a slight temperature increase of 1 degree per day over two days, with a mean of 33.5 C and a maximum of 34 C [E-thermal-0]. The calibrated model indicates elevated risk compared to the fleet base rate across 7, 14, and 30 day windows [E-thermal-1].

Drive 2AGJHTVY shows a rising trend in pending sectors [E-media_health-1] with one increase over two days, while reallocated sectors [E-media_health-0] remain stable. The calibrated family-model risk [E-media_health-3] indicates elevated failure probability compared to the fleet base rate, particularly over the 30-day window, despite no growth in offline uncorrectable sectors [E-media_health-2].

Drive 2AGJHTVY shows a steady power-on increase of 167 hours/day [E-usage_wear-0] and load cycles growing at 1/day [E-usage_wear-2], while power cycles remain static [E-usage_wear-1]. The calibrated model indicates elevated risk compared to the fleet base rate, particularly over the 30-day window [E-usage_wear-3].

Drive 2AGJHTVY shows a stable seek error rate of 100.0 with no increases over the observation window [E-mechanical-0], and zero spin retries [E-mechanical-1]. While the calibrated family-model risk is elevated at 1.51% for both 14-day and 30-day windows compared to the fleet base rate [E-mechanical-2], the lack of mechanical degradation trends suggests the risk is likely due to model calibration rather than imminent failure.

knowledge.text: Media health attributes (SMART 5, 184, 187, 197, 198) / SMART 198: Offline Uncorrectable Sector Count: The total count of uncorrectable errors when reading or writing a sector; a rise indicates defects of the disk surface and/or problems in the mechanical subsystem [1]. In the Google field study, drives were on average 39 times more likely to fail in the 60 days after their first offline uncorrectable error than similar drives without one ([3], as summarized in [1]). SMART 197 and 198 are well correlated in Backblaze data, but not every manufacturer reports both [2].

Media health attributes (SMART 5, 184, 187, 197, 198) / SMART 5: Reallocated Sectors Count: The raw value counts bad sectors that were found and remapped to spare sectors; a higher value means the drive has had to reallocate more sectors [1]. A drive with any reallocations is significantly more likely to fail in the following months [1]. Backblaze investigates a drive when the raw value is greater than zero, but a small isolated value (for example two remapped sectors) means little on its own; it matters in combination with other signals and with how fast it grows [2].

Limits of SMART-based prediction and vendor caveats / Many failures give no SMART warning: In the Google study, 56% of failed drives had no count in the four strongest SMART signals (scan errors, reallocation count, offline reallocation, probational count), and 36% failed with no SMART error at all apart from temperature ([3], as summarized in [1]). Backblaze reports that 23.3% of failed drives showed no warning in its five tracked attributes [2]. A low predicted risk is therefore not a guarantee of health.

data.note: Media health shows a critical increase in pending sectors and reallocated sectors, indicating imminent failure. Usage wear confirms high daily activity correlating with this degradation, while thermal and mechanical metrics show minor or stable trends that are secondary to the media health crisis.
